title: Add support for custom import resolvers in synchronous bundle API
impact: 5 +1 reactions. Reporter maintains an ESLint plugin (ESLint rules must be synchronous) and wanted to resolve `@import "tailwindcss"` from node_modules. Related: #911 (built-in node_modules resolution for bundle(), 0 reactions), #735 (resolver via Vite). Workaround exists: bundleAsync (wrapped synchronously in a worker if needed).
code: napi/src/lib.rs: bundle (native, line ~131) uses FileProvider and ignores `resolver`
napi/src/lib.rs: wasm32 `bundle` (line ~430) already calls a synchronous JS resolver
summary: The native synchronous bundle() always reads from disk; a `resolver` option is silently ignored (the TypeScript types only allow it on bundleAsync). The WASM build's bundle() already accepts a synchronous resolver. Native sync support is harder because the bundler loads imports on rayon worker threads, which cannot call into JS while the JS thread is blocked inside bundle(); it would need a single-threaded path (like WASM) that calls JS directly on the main thread when a resolver is given.
repro: 747-repro.mjs. bundle({filename: '/virtual/main.css', resolver: {read, resolve}}) with virtual files -> `ERROR: No such file or directory (os error 2)`, resolver called 0 times. Control: bundleAsync with the same resolver -> `.pkg{color:#00f}.main{color:red}`.
evidence: scripts/repro.mjs on local (master) + 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1: sync case WRONG everywhere, async control correct everywhere. Code reading of napi/src/lib.rs and src/bundler.rs.

fix.approach: When `resolver` is passed to native bundle(), run the bundle on the calling thread without rayon (or in a 1-thread pool using the current thread) and call read/resolve directly via JsFunction references, as the wasm32 implementation does; reject Promise results with a clear error. Smaller first step: throw a clear error when `resolver` is passed to sync bundle() instead of silently ignoring it.

notVerified: Did not prototype the single-threaded native path or measure its cost. Did not check whether the reporter's plugin still needs this: Tailwind v4 resolves its own `@import`s, so the original use case may be gone.
